1 1.This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed against the award dated 25.6.2014 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dindori in MACC No. 335/2011 by which appellant Insurance Company has been held to be liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: 2. Since the factum of the accident is not in dispute, therefore, it is suffice to mention here that the deceased lost his life in a vehicular accident, which took place on 31.8.2011.

3. Challenging the award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that in fact the offending tractor No. MP-52-AA- 0255 and Trolley No. MP-52-AA-0256 were not insured by the appellant.
4. The claimants had filed a photocopy of the acknowledgement slip.

It is submitted that on 23.1.2014, an application was filed by the appellant seeking direction to the owner to produce the original copy of the acknowledgement slip, which was allowed and accordingly, the owner was directed to produce the original copy of the acknowledgement slip but that was not done, therefore,
an adverse inference may be drawn against the owner.

It is further submitted that the appellant itself has filed the original of all 4 sets of acknowledgement slip and examined Ramraj Vishwakarma (DW-1) to show that the amount of premium was never paid to the appellant, therefore, the acknowledgement slip, which was issued earlier by the agent was cancelled.
Thus, it is submitted that the vehicle in question was not insured and, therefore, liability of the appellant has wrongly been fixed.
5.Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the claimants.

It is submitted by Shri Ghanshyam Sharma that since the original copy of the acknowledgement slip was in possession of the appellant, therefore, the genuineness of the photocopy of the acknowledgement slip filed by the claimants cannot be doubted.

The acknowledgement of receipt of Rs.6900/- is mentioned in the acknowledgement slip (Ex.D-1C), thus it appears that authorized agent of the appellant after recovering the premium amount from the owner did not pass it on to appellant Insurance Company.
No information was given by the Insurance Company to the owner with regard to the non receipt of premium amount.
In these circumstances, the Insurance Company may have some grievance against its own authorized agent but it cannot run away from the liability to pay the compensation amount.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
7.
Appellant Insurance Company itself has filed 4 sets of acknowledgement slip as (Ex.D-1C).

It is the evidence of Ramraj Vishwakarma (DW-1) that since the premium amount was not received,
therefore, the acknowledgement slip was cancelled and no insurance Policy was received.

However,
he was not in a position to disclose the name of agent or the employee, who had issued that acknowledgement slip in which an acknowledgement of receipt of Rs.6900/- was also mentioned.
It was accepted that the company has no Office at Dindori.
It was also accepted that no information was given either to RTO or to vehicle owner with regard to cancellation of acknowledgment slip.

sentences.text: Since appellant Insurance Company itself was in possession of all 4 sets of original acknowledgement slip, therefore, the issuance of acknowledgement slip to the owner is undoubted.
The only question for consideration is as to whether the premium amount was received by the SAN appellant or not.

According to the appellant, the premium amount of Rs. 6900/-
Date: 2023.04.20 18:14:00 IST was not received, therefore, the insurance policy was not issued.

Since the appellant is in possession of all 4 sets of original acknowledgement slip, therefore, it is clear that some authorized agent or some authorized employee of the appellant must have collected the premium amount from the insured/proposed insured and deposited the documents in the office of the appellant.

If the authorized agent or authorized employee, who had acknowledged the receipt of Rs.6900/- in the acknowledgment slip (Ex. D-1C) did not pass it on to the appellant, then it is a matter to be settled by the appellant with its authorized agent or authorized employee.

The Insurance Company cannot take advantage of misdeeds of its own authorized agent or authorized employee specifically when no information with regard to non receipt of premium amount was ever given to the owner or to the RTO.

Under these circumstances, if the insurance company is of the view that it has been cheated by its own authorized agent or authorized employee then it has a remedy to recover the amount from such authorized agent or authorized employee, who had collected premium amount from the owner but the claimants, who were third party, cannot be made to suffer by claiming exoneration on the aforementioned ground.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the Insurance Company is jointly and severally responsible to pay compensation.
No other argument has been advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
9. Accordingly, the award dated 25.6.2014 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dindori in Claim Case No. 335/2011 is hereby affirmed.
The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE PB Hdfc General Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Sampatiya Bai on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52422778/
